title: Half survive, same mix
hook: Track a small population through one event.

knows: An allele is a variant of a gene.
doesNotKnow: Population size can fall while allele frequency stays the same. Other survival samples could change the frequency.

misconception: Population size and allele frequency always change together.
objective: Count allele frequency in a finite haploid population after a specified event.

claims.text: Question, stage and explanation: In a haploid model, each dot is one individual with one A or a allele. Start with 4 A and 4 a. Exactly 2 A and 2 a individuals survive from the starting group. What fraction of the resulting group carries A? The resulting group has 2 A and 2 a, so its A frequency is 2 out of 4. Population size can fall while allele frequency stays the same. Other survival samples could change the frequency. The diagram fixes this one outcome rather than predicting every real population.
claims.source: Specified finite population; biological context: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/19-1-population-evolution

claims.text: Each dot stands for one haploid individual with one allele at this locus; colours do not imply actual organism colours.
Recall: If a haploid group has 2 A individuals and 2 a individuals, what fraction carry A? There are 4 individuals and 2 carry A.
claims.source: Finite count defined by the question.

recall.question: If a haploid group has 2 A individuals and 2 a individuals, what fraction carry A?
recall.why: There are 4 individuals and 2 carry A.
